A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLEMA by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and appendix organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original material-generation experiments across fourteen tasks, component ablations, convergence analyses, and chemical-diversity results.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds MatterGen comparisons, sensitivity and robustness experiments, DFT validation, and computational-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The core generation–oracle–memory loop and Algorithm 1 remain. However, the reported evolutionary rule set decreases from nineteen rules in v1 Appendix D.2 to fourteen in v2 Appendix B.4, removing motif replacement, layered intercalation, structural isomer generation, group-based recombination, and phase-diagram extrapolation. V2 also describes hull stability as a separate check rather than v1's explicitly lower-weighted reward component.

E1.justification: The fourteen materials-discovery task families and application domains remain. V2 extends testing to altered prompt formulations and noisy surrogate feedback in Appendices E.2 and E.5, adding input and feedback conditions within the existing domains. Additional model sizes and DFT checks do not themselves introduce new material tasks.

E2.justification: MatterGen is added as an evaluated comparator across all fourteen tasks in v2 Table 3, using its released base checkpoint. CDVAE, G-SchNet, DiffCSP, End2end, and LLMatDesign remain. Qwen models are LLEMA backbone variants, while MatLLMSearch is discussed without an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: V2 introduces island-count, prompt-variation, Qwen model-size, Gaussian-noise, 150-candidate DFT-validation, and runtime/token evaluation protocols. Existing settings also change: G-SchNet's stated budget rises from 10,000 to 15,000 iterations, and acousto-optic constraints tighten from 2–9 to 3–9 pC/N and dielectric constants from 8–95 to 8–85. Several other benchmark edits reconcile v1 table–appendix disagreements rather than establish newly executed settings; retained scores are not documented as rerun.

E4.justification: V1's component ablations, search trajectories, memorization analysis, and elemental-diversity studies are retained. V2 adds island-count sensitivity in Appendix B.3 and prompt robustness, model scaling, surrogate-versus-DFT reliability, noisy-feedback robustness, and efficiency analyses in Appendices E.2–E.6. These substantially broaden the questions tested about reliability and practical behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for performance. V2's Gaussian perturbations, prompt variants, and DFT validity percentages add experiments and point estimates, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The LLEMA (GPT) hard, stiff ceramics hit rate changes from 60.99 in v1 Table 2 to 30.99 in v2 Table 3; other pre-existing entries in that table retain their values. MatterGen results and Tables 6–10 add substantial findings on sensitivity, model size, validation, and efficiency. Newly reported DFT checks find 144/150 valid candidates under ordinary guidance and 141/150 under noisy guidance; these are added results, not improvements over corresponding v1 measurements.

T1.justification: V1 leaves the normalized reward function unspecified. V2 Appendix B.2 supplies explicit signed, clipped feasibility-margin definitions for lower-bound, upper-bound, and interval constraints, and Equation 2 explicitly includes upper-bound constraints. This adds mathematical specification without introducing a theoretical guarantee or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain chemistry-informed LLM evolution, success/failure memory with multiple islands, constrained multi-objective discovery, and evaluation across fourteen tasks. Both versions claim improved discovery quality, stability, Pareto trade-offs, and reduced memorization. The added studies support these retained claims rather than redefine them; the conclusion is essentially unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of island-count trade-offs, model capacity as a proxy for scientific knowledge, robustness to perturbed oracle feedback, agreement with DFT, and computational cost. These extend the explanation of when and why LLEMA works. The model-scale interpretation attributes gains to domain knowledge without separately isolating that cause, while the conclusion retains the earlier broad limitations.

D1.justification: V2 fills the previously unspecified reward calculation, discloses random sampling of six generation rules, adds a LLEMABench dataset-access link, and provides MatterGen implementation and LLMatDesign feedback details. It also documents Quantum ESPRESSO use, noise parameters, and token/API/runtime costs. These materially improve reproducibility information, although DFT settings are described only as default parameters and some island descriptions remain inconsistent.

R1.justification: V2 adds an introductory framework-comparison table and explicitly positions LLEMA relative to MatterGen and MatLLMSearch. It also adds relevant citations on data scarcity, scientific discovery, Qwen, and Quantum ESPRESSO. The overall research positioning remains; publication updates for already cited works do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: Beyond retitling and copyediting, v2 rewrites substantial introductory and fitness-assessment passages and reorganizes the appendices: additional method details move ahead of the benchmark, and baseline descriptions join the implementation appendix. The main memorization and evolutionary-refinement subsections exchange order. This substantially changes document navigation and exposition while retaining the overall research narrative.

P2.justification: V1's benchmark-overview Figure 1 is removed. V2 adds the framework-comparison table and five analysis tables, expands the main results table with MatterGen rows, and redistributes and enlarges appendix heatmaps. Existing framework, Pareto, convergence, and diversity plots are largely retained or relocated rather than newly generated analyses.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is stronger validation of the central physical-reliability claim: v1 relies on database/surrogate evaluation and plausibility arguments, whereas v2 adds DFT checks reporting 144/150 valid candidates and 141/150 under noisy guidance. Targeted robustness studies and MatterGen comparisons further strengthen the evidence, while explicit reward definitions improve reproducibility. Sparse DFT settings, absent uncertainty estimates, and unresolved protocol inconsistencies limit these gains, but the new validation substantially addresses an important evidential weakness.
